articles.title: A $20 million gift will transform part of Philadelphia's art museum into a new learning centre; the project marks its first major capital expansion since the Frank Gehry renovation
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Museum of Art will transform part of its north wing into a dedicated learning centre following a $20 million gift from philanthropists
articles.body: The Philadelphia Museum of Art will transform part of its north wing into a dedicated learning centre following a $20 million gift from philanthropists Lois G. and Julian A. Brodsky. The project aims to expand educational opportunities for schoolchildren, families and adult learners through dedicated studios, family activities and community spaces. Announced on October 23, 2026, the initiative is among the largest gifts in the museum’s history. It also marks the institution’s first major capital project since architect Frank Gehry’s renovation and expansion reopened in May 2021.The $20 million gift will transform the Philadelphia Museum of ArtAccording to the museum’s official announcement, the new facility will be named the Lois G. and Julian A. Brodsky Learning and Engagement Center, or Brodsky Center. It will transform parts of the north wing into spaces designed specifically for education and public engagement.Initial plans include a family learning centre, art studios, a visitor orientation area and a multipurpose community hub. These facilities will allow visitors to explore art through practical activities and educational programmes, while giving school groups dedicated areas for learning.The museum has appointed Philadelphia-based architecture firm MGA Partners to develop the initial design. The design is expected by summer 2027, while construction is anticipated to be completed within a few years.USA Art News reported that the museum’s existing education facilities cover less than 6,000 square feet. The proposed centre is expected to occupy approximately 19,000 square feet, significantly increasing the space available for educational activities.Why does the museum need more educational spaceThe museum currently welcomes approximately 36,000 students annually, but limited dedicated facilities have restricted its ability to expand educational programmes.According to the museum’s announcement, the new centre will provide additional capacity for school visits, alongside studios and rooms for activities connected to its collection. Existing educational rooms will remain, while some areas currently shared between classes and meetings will become dedicated learning spaces.This arrangement is expected to make it easier to accommodate school groups and organise programmes throughout the day. The centre will also support activities for families, adult learners and community organisations.The museum already offers free admission to visitors aged 18 and younger. It also provides free guided school visits and bus transportation for students from the School District of Philadelphia, its preschools and Head Start programmes, Philadelphia Parks & Recreation camps, and Title I schools across the tri-state region and Delaware Valley.The expansion is intended to build on these efforts and help the museum reach more students. It also reflects the Brodskys’ interest in improving educational access for children and families from underserved communities.How will the centre benefit families and visitorsThe planned centre will offer more than space for organised school trips. Its family learning area and art studios will support hands-on activities, while the visitor orientation area will help people navigate the museum and understand its collection. The multipurpose community hub will provide additional room for gatherings and programmes for different audiences.According to Lifestyles Magazine, the institution has been considering whether to extend its weekday opening hours, as it currently closes on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Any change to the schedule remains under consideration.Brodsky's deep connection with the museumThe donation builds on the couple’s longstanding relationship with the museum. Julian Brodsky, one of the founding principals of telecommunications company Comcast, joined the museum’s board of trustees in 1995. He served as vice-chair from 2003 to 2018 and chaired its audit committee from 2018 to 2023. He became a trustee emeritus in 2024 and continues to serve as vice-chair of the Library and Archives Committee.Lois Brodsky began volunteering at the museum in 1982 as a membership guide. She served as a weekday guide from 1986 to 2019, helping visitors explore the permanent collection and special exhibitions. She currently serves on committees covering conservation, European art, and prints, drawings and photographs.The couple have also supported earlier museum initiatives. According to the official announcement, the Constantin Brancusi gallery was renamed the Lois Green Brodsky Gallery in 2005 in recognition of their contribution to the museum’s 125th-anniversary campaign.In 2009, they also helped establish an endowed photography curator position through the Lenfest Challenge, a fundraising initiative supporting permanent funding for important museum roles. The museum said part of the contribution would support capital improvements, while a portion would be placed in an endowment to help sustain educational work.The Brodsky Center will be the museum’s first major capital project since the Core Project, a four-year renovation and expansion designed by Frank Gehry that reopened in May 2021.You use AI every day. articles.title: Green Card lottery: Judge freezes reopening of Diversity Visa program for 2027. What happens next?
articles.summary: A three-judge panel of the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals Thursday blocked an order that required the Trump administration to reopen the Diversity Visa
articles.body: A three-judge panel of the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals Thursday blocked an order that required the Trump administration to reopen the Diversity Visa lottery. The temporary block means the Diversity Visa program, which is also known as the Green Card lottery, will not open by November 1. The order came as the government requested an injunction staying the previous order, under which the program would have opened. This is another legal setback for the Diversity Visa Program 2027 but Red Eagle Law, the immigration law firm that filed the lawsuit against Secretary of Marco Rubio in August, said they would move forward with other litigation to challenge the State Department's failure to carry out the DV program.Timeline of what exactly happenedDecember 2025: The Trump administration paused the Diversity Visa programAugust 2026: The State Department announced another pause on issuing diversity visas, following a court order that had ended the earlier pause.August 2026: Immigration law firm Red Eagle Law sued the government over its failure to open DV-2027 registration.October 2026: A federal district judge ordered the State Department to reopen DV-2027 registration.October 2026: The Trump administration appealed the ruling and sought to suspend the order.October 2026: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals granted the government's request to temporarily suspend the lower court's order.The stay is a temporary one on the ground that the law firm did not have the legal right to bring the challenge. People who would be affected should approach the court as the Green Card lottery was created to encourage immigration from countries with low US immigration rates, not to generate business for immigration law firms. The judges also pointed out that the firm had not brought the case on behalf of any prospective lottery applicants.Who will be affected?Those who were waiting for the registration to open on November 1.India is not an eligible country for the Green Card lottery, as India's rate of US immigration is high. So Indians do not come under this.What happens next?The State Department is not required to open DV-2027 registration by November 1 because the appeals court has stayed that requirement.The appeal against the district court's preliminary injunction is still pending.The future of the 2027 registration process remains uncertain.Does US want to stop Diversity Visa program?Diversity Visa program admits 55,000 immigrants to the US annually from countries with historically low rates of immigration to the US. The State Department said it was pausing the program as it was undertaking a review of the screening and vetting protocols."The Department of State is committed to ensuring that its visa process upholds the highest standards for US national security and public safety. This action is being taken in light of concerns raised by the shooting at Brown University and killing of an MIT professor suspected to have been committed by an individual admitted to the United States through the DV program. This pause will allow the Department to undertake a review of the screening and vetting protocols in the DV program. This review will address any vulnerabilities in the process to ensure the Department can adequately establish the identity of aliens who are selected through the DV entry lottery, establish the applicants’ visa eligibility, and ensure that they do not present a threat to national security or public safety," the State Department said.The department said they may conduct interviews but no Diversity Visa was being issued.You use AI every day. articles.summary: SRINAGAR: J&K and Ladakh high court sought a compliance report Friday from the Rajouri district administration on its March 25 order to reunite a
articles.body: SRINAGAR: J&K and Ladakh high court sought a compliance report Friday from the Rajouri district administration on its March 25 order to reunite a Pakistan-born teenager deported after the Pahalgam terror attack with his Indian father on grounds of “sacrosanct human values and rights”.Justice MA Chowdhary’s seven-month-old order, iterated by the single-judge bench of Justice Rahul Bharti, equated the boy’s plight with the “human suffering” and estrangement caused by Partition. “The instant case stems out of this tragedy,” the court said, rejecting the Bureau of Immigration’s contention that the boy had been deported because he didn’t have an active visa.Aasim Sajjad, aka Fardin Sajjad, was born to Rajouri-based govt schoolteacher Sajjad Ahmed and a Pakistani woman, Shabnum Kouser of Rawali in Gujranwala. The marriage took place in Pakistan in Dec 2005 and Aasim was born there on Nov 26 the next year.Sajjad’s wife and son visited India in Oct 2007 on a 90-day visa, which was later extended on marital grounds until 2013. When his wife died on June 5, 2013, Ahmed sought an extension of his son’s visa, granted until April 20, 2015. He then purportedly filed repeated applications for Indian citizenship or visa extension on compassionate grounds, none of which was taken up.Ahmed alleged that J&K Police raided his house on April 29, 2025, took his son away in a van and deported him through the Wagah border without informing him or handing over a deportation order. The deportation came after the Union govt cancelled visas to all Pakistani citizens after the April 22 terrorist attack on tourists in Pahalgam and ordered them to leave.In its objections, the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) argued that Ahmed didn’t “come to court with clean hands” and that his son had been staying in India without a valid visa and was legally bound to leave. The FRRO counsel said the status of the teenager’s citizenship application, which Ahmed claims to have filed, remains “not received yet” on the MHA portal.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Rajasthan govt directs all departments to hold 2026-27 DPC promotion meetings by Nov 15, citing delays and reiterating annual seniority timelines.
articles.body: Jaipur: The state govt has directed all departments to complete departmental promotion committee (DPC) meetings for 2026-27 across all cadres by Nov 15, warning that delays are depriving employees of timely promotions.In a circular issued on Oct 28, the department of personnel has asked administrative departments and heads of departments to expedite promotion proceedings, noting that several departments were yet to hold DPC meetings despite the state having granted a relaxation of up to two years in the prescribed experience or service requirements for promotions in Aug 2026.The circular, issued by DOP secretary Archana Singh, reiterated the existing timeline for conducting DPCs, under which departments are required to publish provisional seniority lists as on April 1 by Jan 1, issue final seniority lists by April 1 and complete promotion proceedings by May 31 every year.The personnel department said service rules governing seniority and promotions require departments to prepare and circulate seniority lists annually as of April 1. Based on the availability of vacancies, departments must subsequently convene DPC meetings and initiate promotion proceedings.It also referred to an earlier circular issued on Aug 26, 2023, which laid down the time-bound schedule for completing the exercise.The latest directive follows the state govt’s decision to grant relaxation of up to two years in the prescribed experience or service requirements for promotion in various service rules. The relaxation was notified on Aug 17, 2026, in compliance with an announcement made by the chief minister in the 2026-27 Budget.However, the department observed that DPC meetings for the current financial year had not been conducted in several departments, preventing employees from receiving the benefit of promotions on time.The circular has directed all administrative departments, heads of departments and appointing authorities to ensure that DPC meetings for every cadre are held by Nov 15 and necessary action for promotions is completed.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.body: Jaisalmer: Police Friday seized an SUV carrying 401kg illegal doda post packed in 21 plastic bags in Sindhari police station area of Balotra district.The smugglers, however, abandoned the vehicle and managed to escape after breaking through a barricade.A magazine, three live cartridges and several fake number plates were also recovered from the SUV, raising suspicion about the vehicle's identity and its possible links to an organised smuggling network.Balotra SP Rajesh Kawat said the seizure was made by a police team led by Sindhari SHO Shankarlal Nipu.The operation was launched during routine checking and barricading in view of the ongoing panchayat elections. Police received information that an SUV carrying a consignment of doda post was approaching Sindhari town.Acting on the tip-off, the police team established a blockade in the area and signalled the vehicle to stop. However, the driver allegedly attempted to break through the barricade and flee. Police chased the SUV, but the occupants abandoned the vehicle and escaped on foot.During a subsequent search, police recovered 401kg doda post packed in 21 plastic bags from the vehicle. The SUV, allegedly used for transporting the contraband, was also seized.A further search of the vehicle led to the recovery of a magazine and three live cartridges. Several fake number plates were also found inside the SUV.Police have registered a case at Sindhari police station under Sections 8/15 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, and Sections 3/25 of the Arms Act.According to the SP, a detailed investigation is underway to establish the source of the seized contraband, its intended buyers, the supply chain and the identities of those involved in the smuggling operation. articles.title: HC seeks ED response on man’s torture, forced statement allegations
articles.summary: Telangana High Court seeks ED and police response to petition alleging illegal detention, custodial torture and forced statement in Andhra liquor scam probe; hearing Nov 27.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Telangana high court on Friday sought responses from the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the police on a petition alleging illegal detention and custodial torture by ED officials during questioning in connection with the alleged Andhra Pradesh liquor transportation scam.Justice EV Venugopal directed the ED and the police department to file counters and posted the matter for further hearing on Nov 27.The petition was filed by Mangalampalli Naga Sai Manikanta, who alleged that ED officials detained him for nearly 10 hours at their Hyderabad office on Oct 26, assaulted him and forced him to sign a false statement.Manikanta claimed he was summoned only as a witness and not as an accused in the case. According to the petition, although he appeared before the ED voluntarily, officials questioned him on matters unrelated to him, abused and threatened him, and allegedly assaulted him by twisting his fingers, pulling his ears and pushing him against a wall.He further alleged that businessman Vallu Sandeep, who has a land dispute with his family, entered the interrogation room later in the day and pressured him to state that his family had received black money in a land transaction and to name former minister KV Nageswara Rao and his son K Sunil Kumar. Sandeep allegedly threatened consequences for his family if he refused.Manikanta alleged that he ultimately signed a statement prepared by the officials under physical force and fear without being allowed to read its contents. He has since retracted the statement.In his petition, he sought an independent, court-monitored investigation, preservation of CCTV footage and records from the ED office, registration of an FIR based on his complaint, and a direction restraining authorities from relying on the disputed statement. He has also approached Saifabad police seeking registration of an FIR against the ED officials concerned.Appearing for the ED, counsel Zoheb Hossain opposed the petition, arguing that it was not maintainable. articles.title: Low-pressure, late resumption of water supply post-weekly cut continues across city areas
articles.summary: Pune water supply resumes late with low pressure after weekly Thursday cuts despite PMC repairs; delays, airlocks and tanker shortages hit many areas.
articles.body: Pune: City residents across areas continued to face delays in restoration of water supply and received low-pressure flow in their taps on Friday this time, too, following Thursday’s once-a-week closure.The situation emerged despite PMC having carried out repairs of several air valves and leakages, as well as fixing of air pockets during the closure day, following continuous complaints about restoration of supply ever since weekly cuts were imposed in Pune city on Oct 15.Further, many repair works were completed late on Thursday night, compounding the delay in restoration of supply to some extent on Friday. One such instance occurred in the Patwardhan Baug locality of Erandwane, where a malfunctioning air valve caused a pipeline leakage. Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) washed out water from the entire line to assist repairs, which finished late on Thursday night.Citizens from various areas pointed out that despite this being the third weekly water closure in a row, PMC is yet to streamline and smoothen restoration of supply the following day. Vishal Shinde, a resident of Tanajiwadi in Shivajinagar, said water supply resumes late on Friday evening for them at low pressure. “Every week, people are experiencing two-day water cuts. The civic administration claims to be taking efforts, but progress is very slow,” Shinde said.A similar low-pressure issue was faced in the Satara Road area this Friday. Bhau Kale, a resident of Bibvewadi road, said, “PMC standardly takes at least two days to regularise supply. Water pressure has continued to remain low for us, which is a major hurdle the civic administration will have to tackle in the coming days.”The problem is worse for residents from merged areas, who said there is little improvement in overall water availability for them. Sanjay Satkar, a resident of Hadapsar road, said, “Our area is reeling under water scarcity. Housing societies cannot even get tanker supply on time. We repeatedly have to follow up with local authorities for deployment of tankers. PMC needs to closely monitor this deployment.”PMC’s water supply department officials merely said that work to plug leakages and repair valves to remove airlocks in distribution lines is under way. An official, requesting anonymity, told TOI, “We are clearing the airlocks at maximum locations. Works often face delays owing to various technical reasons. articles.title: Water cuts in Pune likely to get stricter post-Diwali as PMC mulls various options
articles.summary: Pune water cuts may tighten after Diwali as PMC weighs alternate-day supply, reduced hours or 2-day closures; clarity sought on 13 TMC quota till Aug 2027.
articles.body: Pune: Stricter curbs than the ongoing once-weekly water cuts are expected in the city after Diwali this year, with the civic administration currently mulling various options that will allow proper management of available stock till Aug 2027.A revised plan of water cuts will be finalised at a meeting of all-party leaders in PMC soon, to be chaired by city mayor Manjusha Nagpure.Calculations on water supply to PMC till Aug 2027 were expedited on Friday, after Thursday’s Khadakwasla canal committee meeting, where it was decided that the city would get 13 thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of water till then. The civic administration, however, is seeking clarification from the irrigation department on the exact quantum of water the civic body will receive for the next 10 months, as it has consumed around 6 TMC water in the last four months.Sources from the civic body insisted the city should get 13 TMC for the next 10 months as dams currently hold around 24 TMC. “There is no need to take into account the 6.3 TMC that PMC has already consumed in the last four months while calculating the allotted quota for months ahead. If the earlier 6.3 TMC is considered, PMC would get just 7 TMC till Aug. Elected representatives must clear these doubts, else the stock with which the city will have to manage is very less,” said an official, requesting anonymity.Citizens’ group Sajag Nagrik Manch (SNM) has also sought clarification on water quota allotted to PMC. Vivek Velankar of SNM, “Dams supplying to the city are holding 24 TMC of water. If the city is set to get only 7 TMC for the next 10 months, how does the rest of it get accounted for? We need clarity. Drinking water requirements need to get top priority.”Civic officials said the final calculations would be done based on water availability, but it is for certain that water cuts will be increased. Options being explored include alternate-day supply, reducing existing supply hours and imposing water closure on two days a week.There has been pushback from residents to implementing alternate-day water supply, as Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) had failed to execute this plan effectively during the previous round of water cuts implemented in June this year.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: In 2025, Maryland professor Anne Simon pledged $16 million for endowed professorships and scholarships at her university
articles.summary: In a groundbreaking move, University of Maryland professor Anne Simon pledged $16 million to enhance research, education, and scholarships in the fields of virology and plant biology, following her own experiences with funding challenges.
articles.body: Seven years before she announced her decision to gift millions of dollars to the University of Maryland, a gap between federal research grants had put Professor Anne Simon in a position of losing her laboratory. At the time, the virologist was en route to develop a treatment for a disease that threatened citrus trees, and help from her department was what kept the laboratory going. In November 2025, with her own experience of the funding crisis behind her, she decided to take on a commitment that would help other researchers to avoid the same problem.According to the University of Maryland’s College, Simon is donating $15 million to support two endowed professorships, postdoctoral fellowships, and graduate fellowships. The professorships will focus on virology and RNA or plant biology. The remaining $1 million in hand would support the Sondra Simon Memorial Maryland Promise Scholarship, named after her mother, who was a teacher’s aide in Los Angeles public schools for more than 30 years. The commitment also forms part of the university’s Forward: The University of Maryland Campaign for the Fearless, and Simon’s contribution brought the campaign’s total to $943 million as it officially launched.Speaking on her decision, she said “I want to pay it back,” she said in the university’s announcement, adding, “I owe it all to my department.” She also emphasised that her objective was to retain established researchers and, at the same time, bring in new ones, particularly junior faculty members.Simon co-founded a company working on citrus greening Simon’s work outside of the University gave her the financial means to be able to undertake a huge commitment. She co-founded Silvec Biologics, a company committed to developing a way to combat citrus greening disease, alongside her brother, Rafael Simon. Citrus greening is a bacterial infection that has caused extensive damage to citrus production in Florida. The disease was first documented in the United States back in 2005, and more than 90% of oranges and grapefruits have been decimated since. Moreover, it had also been making its way across parts of Asia, the Americas, and AfricaThe approach to counter this disease that existed until that point involved injecting trees with medical-grade antibiotics. At Silvec, the methodology took a different approach; instead of relying on the existing methods, it used an RNA virus to deliver antimicrobial peptides into the trees through a vaccination approach. The method has so far proved effective under laboratory testing, while field testing was in motion when the university published its November 2025 account.Silvec’s technology isn’t only defined by the method it offers but also has applications that go beyond citrus. The technology could also be applied to row crops such as wheat and soybeans, potentially reducing the need for fungicides and pesticides. Simon joined the University of Maryland in 2000 and subsequently created the department’s virology programme, which she has led, according to department chair Kevin S. McIver. Her work portfolio includes research in RNA biology and collaborations with scientists at the National Institutes of Health, and an inter-institutional graduate programme to attract students to the field.From laboratory science to The X-FilesSimon’s scientific work has also extended into television. She advised The X-Files, the Fox science-fiction series about FBI agents investigating paranormal cases, helping its writers keep scientific details credible even when the plots involved fictional organisms and extraordinary events.A 2016 University account says Simon began advising the creator of the show, Chris Carter, during the programme’s original run. Their connection had developed after Simon watched the show’s first episode in 1993 and recognised Carter’s name through a family connection.Carter sought her advice on how scientists might handle an unfamiliar bacterial strain, for which Simon suggested growing additional samples and using laboratory equipment suited to study the organism, which involved the use of an Erlenmeyer flask and a scanning electron microscope. In January 2016, when the series returned on screen for a six-episode revival, she again provided scientific advice, and it was recognised in the form of her first Hollywood story credit for a plot developed for the final episode. Simon wrote The Real Science Behind ‘The X-Files’, published in 1999, and used the programme as an opportunity to make science fiction stories more credible.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mandsaur resident held for supplying MD drugs and dodachura to two Gujarat men caught with contraband earlier this week
articles.summary: Mandsaur police arrested Dilnawaz for allegedly supplying 100g MD drugs and 8kg dodachura to two Gujarat men held with contraband worth Rs 27.66 lakh.
articles.body: Indore: Mandsaur police arrested a Khanpura resident late Thursday for allegedly supplying MD drugs and dodachura to two Gujarat men caught with the contraband earlier this week.Kotwali police station in-charge Pushpendra Singh Rathore said Dilnawaz was arrested after the two accused reportedly identified him as their supplier. Police are questioning him to trace the source of the drugs and identify others allegedly involved in their movement and distribution.Kotwali police intercepted a black SUV near Harsh Eco City Colony in Abhinandan Nagar on Tuesday. A search yielded 100 grams of MD drugs and eight kg of dodachura.The occupants, Mohsin (32) and Rohan alias Rehan (22), are from Gujarat. Police said the seized contraband, vehicle and an iPhone were collectively valued at Rs 27.66 lakh.During questioning, the men allegedly said they had travelled to Mandsaur to procure the drugs from Dilnawaz, who was subsequently arrested in Khanpura, Rathore said.Investigators are examining how Dilnawaz obtained the drugs, his contacts, whether the consignment had a specific destination in Gujarat and the possible involvement of others in the supply chain.The Gujarat residents, booked at Kotwali police station, are in police custody till Oct 31.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Indore | Silver Rate in Indore | Bank Holidays in Indore | Public Holidays in Indore | Petrol Price in Indore | Diesel Price in Indore | CNG Price in Indore | LPG Price in IndoreStay updated with the latest Indore news.
